title: Redwood POC Weekly Sync - Benchmark Review vs Baseline Provider
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results (latency/throughput) comparing Redwood to the customer's baseline provider. Discussed tuning knobs (batching, quantization, KV/prefix cache), dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, and next steps for expanded benchmark and security docs. Agreed actions: run 95th percentile latency tests with realistic traffic pattern, try quantized model profile from Redwood, and schedule on-prem network test next week.
topics: Differences vs baseline provider -- tail latency and CPU vs GPU bottlenecks
Tuning options: batching, kv cache, sequence length profiles, quantization
Deployment modes: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC)
Security/compliance ask: audit logs, SOC2, KMS integration
action_items: Owner: Kenji Sato; Item: Run 95th percentile tail-latency benchmark with production-like fanout and sequence lengths; Due: 2026-12-08
Owner: Sara Gomez; Item: Provide representative prompt set and delta distribution for sequence lengths (chat vs doc summarize); Due: 2026-12-03
Owner: Ava Martinez; Item: Share Redwood security whitepaper, SOC2 evidence summary, and KMS integration guide; Due: 2026-12-04
Owner: Liam O'Connor; Item: Arrange access for on-prem network throughput test and firewall rules; Due: 2026-12-10
next_steps: Run p95 benchmark with realistic concurrency and share raw logs (Kenji)
Customer to send prompt distribution and test corpus (Sara)
Redwood to provision quantized model profile and dedicated GPU pool for next test (Ava/Kenji)
Schedule a network/latency check for private deployment early next week (Liam)
Redwood to send SOC2 + KMS docs and pricing delta for dedicated capacity (Ava)
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, popping on, uh, happy Tuesday. this is our weekly sync to go over the benchmark numbers versus your baseline provider. we pulled the latest runs last night.
[00:08] Priya Nair: Thanks Ava. we only have 45 minutes, so big picture then dive into p95 numbers please.
[00:14] Kenji Sato: Cool. I'll share screen in a sec, but quick TL;DR: Redwood matched baseline on p50 across most tests, improved p95 tail by ~18% on the chat-heavy workload when using KV prefix caching and our continuous batching. throughput for steady-state long sequences was similar, baseline edged out slightly on raw token/sec for very small sequence lengths due to their optimized CPU path.
[00:35] Liam O'Connor: when you say baseline edged out, is that on single-GPU or multi-node? we run multi-node shards in prod.
[00:41] Kenji Sato: The baseline numbers were on their multi-node sharded setup. our comparison used a single Redwood dedicated instance and a single baseline node to keep configuration parity; we also ran a multi-node Redwood pool test which is in the appendix.
[00:54] Sara Gomez: you mentioned KV prefix cache — can you remind us how that helps tail latency? we noticed big spikes in p95 during conversational resets.
[01:02] Kenji Sato: Yeah, so KV cache avoids recomputing full prefixes on repeated prompt patterns. in chat workloads where users often re-use system prompts or context windows, the runtime reuses the cached KV layers which reduces compute and dramatically shortens tail latency for subsequent requests. that's why p95 improved on chat-heavy tests.
[01:22] Priya Nair: show us numbers please.
[01:24] Kenji Sato: Sure, ok numbers slide: baseline provider p50 ~ 120 ms, p95 ~ 540 ms for short chat-turns (<=128 tokens). Redwood hosted p50 ~ 118 ms, p95 ~ 440 ms with caching enabled. dedicated Redwood quantized profile p50 ~125 ms, p95 ~ 410 ms. throughput: baseline sustained ~ 650 tokens/s per node on short sequences, Redwood dedicated ~630 tokens/s per GPU, multi-node pooling scales linearly in our tests.
[01:49] Liam O'Connor: 540 to 440 is decent. what's the variability? like stdev or wide outliers?
[01:54] Kenji Sato: In our logs the baseline had heavier right-tail — occasional spikes to 1.2s under cold cache conditions. Redwood's continuous batching adds small jitter at p50 but keeps tails lower because of cache + earlier kernel selection. variance numbers are in the CSV we shared, but median variance is comparable.
[02:12] Sara Gomez: ok. I see you said quantized profile — how much accuracy drop did you see with int8-ish quantization? our NLU tests are sensitive.
[02:20] Kenji Sato: Good question. For the Llama-variant we're using as a proxy, quantization to 8-bit showed <0.7% delta in Rouge/F1 on our eval set. we ran a targeted accuracy check with your sample prompt set; differences were within noise for classification/regression, but we flagged a few failure modes on edge cases — we'll share the eval report.
[02:41] Priya Nair: Are those evals using your standardized prompt suite or our real prompt distribution?
[02:46] Kenji Sato: A mix — the internal eval is standardized, but for the run last night we used the prompt set you provided last cycle plus some synthetic long-context cases. Sara, can you send the final prompt distribution so we can run full quantization-sensitive evals?
[02:56] Sara Gomez: Yep I'll upload the corpus after this.
[02:59] Ava Martinez: Quick security check — Priya you had asked about audit logs and KMS earlier in the thread. we have SOC2 and support KMS integrations for dedicated/private. I'll send the whitepaper after the call.
[03:10] Priya Nair: Good. Liam needs details on VPC peering and egress.
[03:14] Liam O'Connor: Correct — for private deployment we need to simulate our firewall rules. who will coordinate?
[03:18] Ava Martinez: We can provision a temporary private test env. Liam, if you give us the IP ranges and the firewall rules, Kenji can run a small network throughput test next week.
[03:27] Liam O'Connor: I'll open a ticket with security ops today.
[03:30] Kenji Sato: Back to performance — we also tried dynamic kernel selection. for long sequences (>=1024 tokens) Redwood's kernel compiles path picks a path that favors memory throughput which helps throughput but adds a touch to p50 latency. baseline's CPU optimized path handles many short requests very efficiently which is why they had the tiny throughput edge at very small seq lengths.
[03:57] Priya Nair: Is there an easy way to tune for our mix — about 70% short chat turns, 30% longer doc summarization?
[04:04] Kenji Sato: Absolutely. We typically recommend: 1) enable prefix/KV caching for the chat-heavy flows, 2) set a batching window of 8–12 ms for short-turn optimization, 3) use a mixed profile: quantized for doc summarization workers where cost matters, dedicated full-precision pools for utterance-critical chat paths. You can route by endpoint or use our smart routing policies.
[04:24] Sara Gomez: how hard is that split in practice? our infra team wants minimal operational complexity.
[04:28] Ava Martinez: We can manage routing in the Redwood Console; you tag routes and set autoscaling rules per route. Kenji's team can set up initial templates so you get copy-paste configs.
[04:36] Liam O'Connor: what about cost delta for dedicated vs hosted? we need runway numbers.
[04:40] Ava Martinez: I'll follow up with a pricing delta for the dedicated pool and the expected per-token cost with and without quantization. For roughs, dedicated committed pricing gives you a lower per-token cost at the expense of commit. We'll include examples for your current traffic.
[04:51] Priya Nair: Can we get a sanity check on SLOs — if p95 is target 500 ms, what guarantees do we get with dedicated?
[04:58] Kenji Sato: With dedicated we hit predictable throughput and we can promise 99.9% availability; tail latency SLOs are tied to chosen hardware profile and batching rules. We'll propose a canary config that meets p95 <= 450 ms for your chat profile in the next run.
[05:12] Sara Gomez: quick aside — did you test context window preservation across multi-turns? we've seen regressions when session persistence drops.
[05:19] Kenji Sato: Yes, session-level KV persistence was on in the POC. drops only occurred when we explicitly flushed the cache during the cold start scenarios; otherwise we maintain kv for session duration.
[05:30] Ava Martinez: I'm going to open the security doc again: we provide per-request audit logs, SSO/SAML, role-based access control, and KMS for key management. we'll send the SOC2 summary and the audit log format.
[05:42] Priya Nair: that's helpful. Liam, any blockers on networking for the scheduled tests?
[05:46] Liam O'Connor: I need to validate a couple of firewall egress paths with security — should be ok but I'll confirm by Friday.
[05:52] Kenji Sato: On instrumentation, we'll share Grafana dashboards for latency and throughput and provide Prometheus metrics endpoints. If you want we can also push sample traces into your tracing backend.
[06:02] Sara Gomez: yes please, tracing would help debug the p95 spikes.
[06:06] Kenji Sato: noted. We'll enable tracing for the next run.
[06:09] Ava Martinez: Any other questions before we go to the detailed slides?
[06:13] Priya Nair: No, go ahead Kenji.
[06:15] Kenji Sato: (slides) moving on to the raw CSV appendix — we ran 10k requests at 50 concurrent workers, distribution matched last week's provided pattern except we added a cold-start batch. Chart 1 shows p50/p95 across 3 runs. Run A (baseline) p95 540ms, Run B (Redwood hosted w/ cache) p95 440ms, Run C (Redwood dedicated quantized) p95 410ms.
[06:40] Kenji Sato: Note the throughput drop during long sequences was ~4% for quantized due to reordering and extra dequant steps but cost dropped ~22% for the same workload.
[06:52] Sara Gomez: 22% cost drop is attractive if accuracy holds. we'll need the eval report.
[06:56] Kenji Sato: We'll attach it in the follow-up. Also performance delta under multi-tenant load is in the multi-node appendix — we saw near linear scaling up to 8 GPUs.
[07:08] Priya Nair: did you test with our spike profile — 3x traffic bursts?
[07:12] Kenji Sato: Yes, in the burst test Redwood's smart routing routed lower-priority batches to quantized pool and kept chat endpoints on dedicated low-latency pool, which kept p95 within SLO for high-priority traffic. baseline handled bursts with auto-sharding but had higher tail due to queueing.
[07:27] Liam O'Connor: the smart routing sounds interesting — how configurable is it?
[07:29] Kenji Sato: You can define route policies by header, user tier, or model tag. you can set fallbacks and capacity thresholds. We can give you a policy template.
[07:37] Sara Gomez: ok. On the next run can we include a test where we intentionally disable KV cache to see worst-case p95? We want to understand our worst-case user experience.
[07:45] Kenji Sato: Absolutely, we'll run both cached and cold-cache scenarios.
[07:49] Ava Martinez: Great. Quick recap of decisions: 1) Redwood to run p95 tail benchmark with production-like fanout and burst patterns; 2) run quantized evaluation against Sara's prompt set; 3) enable tracing and share dashboards; 4) Redwood to send security docs and pricing. Anything to add?
[08:08] Priya Nair: Add on-prem network test coordination.
[08:11] Ava Martinez: noted.
[08:13] Priya Nair: ok schedule the next sync same time next week.
[08:16] Ava Martinez: will do. Thanks everyone.
[08:19] (call ends)
